text: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
My soul waits in silence for God alone; from him comes my salvation.
He alone is my rock and my salvation, my stronghold; I will never be badly shaken.
How long will you all assail a man, to break him down as though he were a leaning wall, a tottering fence?
They plot only to bring him down from his high place; they take pleasure in falsehood. With their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah

versions.text: They plot only to topple him from his height; they delight in lies. With their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah
versions.explanation: "Topple him from his height" is slightly awkward for oral reading, and "delight in lies" is better matched to יִרְצוּ כָזָב as "take pleasure in falsehood," keeping the rhythm smoother.

versions.text: They plot only to bring him down from his high place; they take pleasure in falsehood.
versions.explanation: The final clauses of the Hebrew verse — בְּפִיו יְבָרֵכוּ ('with his/their mouth they bless'), וּבְקִרְבָּם יְקַלְלוּ ('and inwardly they curse'), and the liturgical marker סֶלָה ('Selah') — are entirely absent from the current text. Roughly half the verse has been dropped. The wording is restored from the earlier revision, which the previous editorial pass had retained.

text: Be silent before God alone, my soul, for my hope comes from him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation, my stronghold; I will not be shaken.
My salvation and my honor rest on God; my mighty rock, my refuge, is in God.

versions.text: My salvation and my honor rest on God; he is my mighty rock, my refuge.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew ends with בֵּאלֹהִים ("in God"), which the current rendering drops, and it adds "he is" which is not in the text. The suggested wording preserves the closing emphasis on God.

versions.text: My salvation and my honor rest on God; my mighty rock, my refuge is in God.
versions.explanation: In the Hebrew, "the rock of my strength" and "my refuge" stand in apposition, both completed by "in God." Without a comma after "my refuge," the English can be misread as two separate clauses ("my mighty rock" left hanging). The added comma clarifies the apposition and gives the line a clearer cadence when read aloud.

text: Trust in him at all times, you people; pour out your hearts before him. God is our refuge. Selah
Those of low estate are only a breath, those of high estate a lie; placed on the scales, they go up; together they are lighter than a breath.

versions.text: Mortals are only a breath, the children of men a delusion; weighed in the balance they rise, together they are less than nothing.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew contrasts בְּנֵי־אָדָם (common people) with בְּנֵי אִישׁ (people of rank); "mortals" and "children of men" lose the contrast. Also מֵהֶבֶל יָחַד means "together lighter than a breath," echoing הֶבֶל at the start, not "less than nothing."

text: Do not trust in extortion, or set vain hopes on stolen goods; if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.

versions.text: Do not trust in extortion or set vain hopes on robbery; if your wealth increases, do not set your heart on it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew חַיִל is impersonal ("riches"), not "your wealth"; the plural pronoun also reads more naturally aloud.

text: Once God has spoken, twice I have heard it: power belongs to God,
and to you, O Lord, belongs steadfast love; for you repay each one according to what he has done.
